items.title: No local explanation for the variation
items.whyItMatters: The five sites are known to differ, but not why, so any strategy chosen now would be a guess.
items.opportunity: Compare staff accounts at higher- and lower-performing sites selected from network figures.

items.title: Night-time care is rarely studied
items.whyItMatters: Performance is worst at night everywhere (claim c2), yet few studies examine it separately.
items.opportunity: Sample night-shift staff at every site and observe at least one night shift per site.

items.title: Performance figures are recorded differently
items.whyItMatters: Recognition time is recorded differently between hospitals, so site rankings may be unreliable.
items.opportunity: Use the figures to select contrasting sites, not to rank them, and check recording practice during fieldwork.

items.title: Smaller sites and night patients get slower care
items.whyItMatters: The day-night gap is largest in smaller hospitals, so patients in rural areas and those arriving at night bear the delay.
items.opportunity: Include the smallest site and report determinants for night care separately.

errorsFound: The request implies the weaker sites lack knowledge of the bundle; the retrieved evidence suggests knowledge is similar and the differences lie in protocols, access and staffing.
reevaluation: The gaps point to an explanatory multi-site study of determinants before any strategy is chosen.
summary: Four gaps: no local explanation, night care, recording differences, and slower care at smaller sites and at night.
